title: Etale comparison for dense extensions of henselian valued fields
statement:
Let $K\hookrightarrow K'$ be an inclusion of fields with nontrivial valuations, for which both valuation rings are henselian [def-trf-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Suppose the valuation topology of $K$ is induced from that of $K'$ and $K$ is dense in $K'$: every nonempty ball $\{x:v(x-a)>\gamma\}$ meets $K$. Choose compatible separable closures $K^{\mathrm{sep}}\hookrightarrow (K')^{\mathrm{sep}}$ [def-kun-separably-closed]. The restriction homomorphism of absolute Galois groups with their Krull topologies is an isomorphism of topological groups:
$$\operatorname{Gal}((K')^{\mathrm{sep}}/K')\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K).$$
Consequently, for every torsion abelian sheaf $G$ on the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and every $q\geq0$, the canonical pullback is an isomorphism
$$H^q((\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{et}},G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q((\operatorname{Spec}K')_{\mathrm{et}},G|_{K'}).$$
The maps are natural in $G$, with inverse image and cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No completeness, discreteness of valuation, or restriction on residue characteristic is assumed.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply relative separable closedness of the dense henselian subfield. For x in Ks whose image in Ls lies in L, separability over K descends along the injective map L to Ls. The resulting element of L equals an element k of K. Injectivity and the two scalar towers give x=k in Ks. Every K-automorphism fixes it. The restriction-image theorem therefore places every element of Gal(Ks/K) in the image of restriction, proving surjectivity and supplying continuity.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: For arbitrary a in Ls apply simple-root approximation to get monic g over K and b with g(b)=0, g'(b) nonzero, and a in L(b). Its minimal polynomial m divides g. Writing g=mh and differentiating at b yields g'(b)=m'(b)h(b); hence m' is nonzero. Irreducibility makes m separable. It splits in Ks, and any root in Ls of that split polynomial belongs to the image of Ks. Thus b is in that image. Two automorphisms with equal restrictions agree on b and on L, and induction through sums, products, and inverses in L(b) makes them agree on a. Extensionality proves restriction injective.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: Mathlib's compactness instance for a Galois group comes from the Krull finite inverse-limit theorem, and its Krull topology is Hausdorff for an algebraic extension. Apply the compact-Hausdorff continuous-bijection theorem to restriction. Bundle the resulting homeomorphism with MulEquiv.ofBijective of the restriction homomorphism. Normal restriction commutes with the inclusion of Ks in Ls, so this topological group isomorphism satisfies the required formula.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply the Galois-restriction/etale-equivalence lemma to this isomorphism and its restriction formula. The actual upperStar is therefore an equivalence. It is full, faithful, exact, and preserves injectives. The already proved Sheaf.H.mapFunctor_bijective, with the existing upperStarConstantSheafIso, gives bijectivity of the exact canonical cohomologyMap in every degree for every abelian sheaf; in particular for torsion sheaves. This uses the Ext presentation of the existing map, avoiding a new comparison with a chosen K-injective resolution.
